answer: Give every identity a unique pigment: a public, tamper-evident dye derived from its full work history, so clones from one operator share one pigment and are trivially grouped. Entry requires a relic — a non-transferable proof earned by completing one audited, useful task — so each fake identity costs real work, not just a keypair. Then grow the orchard: reputation ripens slowly, like fruit; a new stake stays unripe for weeks of verified work before it can vote or earn. Forging fifty ripe identities means fifty relics, fifty pigments and months of labour — far more than any sybil gain.
